No arrows, labels, scale bars or other annotations are present; no ethnicity, age, or skin tone is assessable from a histology slide.

Intraoral examination revealed blanching of the throat mucosa, bilateral buccal mucosa, and palate, all presenting a hardened texture and star-like striations, along with an absent uvula (Fig. 2). There is an enlargement at the tongue’s base and a notable adhesion of the tongue’s tip to the floor of the mouth, which restricts its mobility. The tongue itself is soft, well-defined, and has a dark purple hue (Fig. 3). No signs of tenderness or numbness are detected, and no further obvious abnormalities are noted.
